# sv0 VS Code / Cursor extension: delivery plan

## purpose

Plan — **not yet implement** — an independently versioned VS Code/Cursor extension for
`sv0`, governed by the product/engineering specification at
`~/Documents/project-specs/sv0-vsc-extension/SPEC.md` (source-audit date
2026-08-22; audited revisions: `sv0-toolchain@8a1eeb2`, `sv0c@ac272be`,
`sv0doc@451fcd9`, `sv0vm@504eeaa`, `sv0-mcp@6ef9926`). This file is the **hub**:
scope, architecture, phase sequencing, gates, and open decisions. The trackable
**`VSC-S-###`** slice backlog lives in **`task/sv0-vsc-extension-checklist.Rmd`**.

This is a **separate product** from the `sv0-toolchain` design-milestone roadmap
(`task/sv0-toolchain-roadmap-full.Rmd`, milestones 0–6): the extension is its own
repository (AE-003) consuming `sv0-toolchain`/`sv0c`/`sv0doc`/`sv0vm` as read-only
upstream authorities. No `roadmap_parent` is set on this file for that reason —
link from here, don't nest under the compiler roadmap.

## where we start (2026-08-22)

- **No extension repository exists yet.** The spec is a governing draft; nothing
  in `sv0-vsc-extension/` has been scaffolded.
- **No `sv0-lsp` exists.** The audit found no LSP server, no machine-readable
  general diagnostic schema, no editor-safe in-memory `check`, no AST formatter,
  no DAP, no cross-platform installed-toolchain layout, and **no license files**
  in any of the five audited repos.
- **What upstream already gives us for free (F0 can build on this without a
  server):** a normative EBNF grammar + keyword/operator reference (`sv0doc`),
  compiler source spans (file/line/col/byte-offset), stable `E####` diagnostic
  codes on a curated rejection corpus, single-file + recursive project
  compilation, `sv0 verify --json`, a conservative whitespace formatter
  (`scripts/fmt_sv0.py`), and a learning-examples corpus.
- **Consequence (spec §4.3):** two-layer delivery. F0 ships safe declarative
  support with zero semantic pretense; R0.1 adds semantic intelligence only
  through a compiler-backed, versioned LSP contract. The extension **never**
  scrapes human stderr or embeds a second parser/type-checker (AE-002).

## scope decisions (locked by the spec)

1. **Architecture = thin TypeScript client + out-of-process `sv0-lsp` over LSP/stdio** (AE-001). Runs on the workspace host (local or remote extension host).
2. **No semantic fallback parser** (AE-002) — missing/incompatible server ⇒ disabled features + one actionable status, never regex-emulated intelligence.
3. **Independent extension repository**, read-only upstream authorities, generated fixtures are reviewed changes (AE-003).
4. **Stable common `vscode` APIs only through R1**; Cursor-specific APIs are a separate future decision (AE-004).
5. **No bundled upstream executable** (`sv0c`/`sv0vm`/`sv0-lsp`/Z3/scripts) until licensing is explicit and reviewed (AE-005, PKG-008).
6. **Canonical distribution = official VS Code Marketplace** under one extension ID, published via GitHub Actions OIDC trusted publishing — no steady-state PAT (AE-010, AE-011).

formatter style contract) that hasn't happened yet.

## decisions record

Resolved 2026-08-22, in order:

- **OD-001.** Repository: `github.com/sv0-toolchain/sv0-vsc-extension` (same org
  as `sv0c`/`sv0doc`/`sv0vm`/`sv0-mcp`). Marketplace publisher ID:
  `sv0-toolchain` (immutable once created — matches the GitHub org for
  consistent branding). `package.json.name`: `sv0-lang`. `displayName`: `sv0`.
  **Canonical extension identifier: `sv0-toolchain.sv0-lang`** — treat as
  public API from the moment the publisher first publishes under it.
- **OD-002.** Extension source license: **MIT**.
- **OD-003.** All five audited upstream repos (`sv0-toolchain`, `sv0c`,
  `sv0doc`, `sv0vm`, `sv0-mcp`) now carry `LICENSE-APACHE` + `LICENSE-MIT`
  (dual Apache-2.0/MIT, the standard Rust-ecosystem pattern) under the user's
  copyright — confirmed present at repo root of each on 2026-08-22. Fixture
  copying (GOV-001/TEST-002 provenance still required) and future upstream
  binary bundling (PKG-008, still gated on an explicit redistribution review)
  are unblocked.
- **OD-004.** `sv0-lsp` lives **inside `sv0c`** as a component/binary reusing
  the compiler front end directly — no cross-repo API boundary, versioned
  together with `sv0c` releases. Governed by the `sv0c` maintainers.
- **OD-005.** `engines.vscode` floor: **`>=1.85.0`**.
- **OD-008.** Release workflow: **`.github/workflows/publish-vscode.yml`**.
  Protected Marketplace environment: **`vscode-marketplace`** — matches the
  spec's own runbook example verbatim (§26.6), so the runbook stays directly
  copy-pasteable.

Still-open follow-up **actions** (not decisions) this unblocks but does not
itself complete: creating the `sv0-toolchain` Marketplace publisher record and
confirming `sv0-lang`/`sv0` availability (VSC-S-007), configuring the
trusted-publishing policy + GitHub protected environment (VSC-S-008), and
recording publisher owners/recovery contacts (VSC-S-009) — these need a human
in the Marketplace publisher-management portal and GitHub org settings, not
just a decision.

Per-epic engineering-note sub-tasks (`task/sv0-vsc-extension-<epic>.Rmd`, mirroring

## design/risk notes carried from the spec

- **Compiler accuracy over plausibility.** Every semantic answer traces to the
  shared compiler pipeline; a wrong `[verified]`-style false-positive is a
  soundness bug, not a UX nit (same discipline as `sv0 verify`, see
  `task/sv0-toolchain-milestone-4-verification.Rmd`).
- **Byte offsets vs UTF-16.** The compiler stores byte offsets; LSP positions are
  UTF-16. Centralize conversion (`VSC-S-214`) with non-BMP property tests —
  spec calls this out as risk #4 (§24).
- **Diagnostic storms while typing.** Batch/incremental-version assumptions,
  cancellation, and a cascade budget (`DIA-007`) prevent UI thrash.
- **Command injection surface.** All external process invocation (server spawn,
  future `sv0`/`z3` CLI actions) uses argv arrays + `shell: false`, trust-gated,
  with an adversarial path corpus (`SEC-005`, `SEC-006`, `TOOL-005`).
- **Marketplace identity is the real blast radius.** A compromised publisher or
  release workflow can push updates to every installed user; OIDC scoped to
  `contents: read` + `id-token: write`, a protected environment, and two-person
  approval for any unpublish/removal are non-negotiable (`SEC-015`–`SEC-017`).
- **Tested artifact ≠ published artifact** is an explicit failure mode: publish
  only via `vsce publish --packagePath` on the checksum-identified candidate,
  never rebuild between test and publish (`PKG-013`).

## completion criteria per gate

- **F0 (§21.1):** PKG-001…006 + PKG-010…012; LANG-001…010; FMT-001…004;
  SEC-001/002/007/010/011/016; COMP-001 across VS Code + Cursor + web; no
  semantic feature advertised; README/CHANGELOG/LICENSE/SECURITY/SUPPORT exist;
  publisher + canonical ID + trusted-publishing policy + protected environment
  configured; packaged VSIX matches the source tag and allowlist.
- **R0.1 (§21.2):** upstream `sv0-lsp` satisfies LS0–LS2 + LSP-001…016;
  diagnostic/project/navigation/semantic-token/server-formatting requirements
  pass; Workspace Trust + process-invocation security tests pass; VS Code +
  Cursor evidence recorded independently; performance budgets pass on the
  declared reference machine; known semantic gaps documented, never
  client-fabricated; no unlicensed upstream binary in public artifacts;
  PKG-009 + PKG-013…016, SEC-015…017, TEST-011…012 pass; exact tested artifact
  is a discoverable, installable Marketplace pre-release.
- **R1 (§21.3):** two consecutive R0.x releases with no unresolved
  data-loss/injection/crash-loop/semantic-corruption defect; LSP conformance +
  upgrade/migration tests; support/deprecation policy; signed provenance
  artifacts; PKG-017 + TEST-013 pass for the regular release + supported
  pre-release upgrade; 30-minute soak clean; accessibility sign-off; no
  unresolved severity-critical/high security finding.

## phases

### phase 0: governance and feasibility

/ai: resolve OD-001…003, OD-005, OD-008; create the Marketplace publisher ID and
confirm name/display-name availability; configure the trusted-publishing policy
and protected `vscode-marketplace` GitHub environment; create the
compatibility-baseline manifest and fixture-provenance format. No extension code
before this closes.

### phase 1: F0 lexical vertical slice

/ai: scaffold the TypeScript extension per spec §10; author the TextMate grammar
and language configuration from the audited `sv0doc` grammar/keyword reference;
add provenance-backed snippets; implement pure phase-0 formatting identical to
`scripts/fmt_sv0.py`; build the complete Marketplace listing assets; pass the
F0 gate from the packaged VSIX.

### phase 2: language-server protocol foundation

/ai: specify `sv0ProtocolVersion` negotiation and `sv0-lsp --version --format=json`
output; stand up the client transport (stdio JSON-RPC, argv spawn, discovery
precedence, cancellation, UTF-16 conversion, bounded restart); build the
differential compiler/server fixture harness and an LSP conformance mock-server
harness. Depends on OD-004 and upstream UP-002/UP-003.

### phase 3: R0.1 language intelligence

/ai: implement symbols/hover/definition/references/completion/signature-help/
rename/workspace-symbols/semantic-tokens against the real server; add AST
formatting only if OD-007 is resolved; harden security/compat/performance/
accessibility; publish the exact tested VSIX as the public Marketplace
pre-release and retain post-publication evidence (TEST-011/012).

### phase 4: R0.2 workflows

/ai: stabilize an installed `sv0` CLI contract and JSON schemas (depends on
UP-007/UP-008); add explicit verify/build/run/task workflows gated on trust;
add only diagnostic-code-backed quick fixes; evaluate hierarchies/hints/Test
Explorer/signed toolchain acquisition separately, each with its own
requirement + threat model + compatibility row.

### phase 5: R1 stabilization

/ai: close Preview reliability/UX findings; complete protocol/deprecation
policy and migrations; establish signing/SBOM/provenance/support/security
response; test the Marketplace pre-release-to-stable upgrade path; publish the
exact tested R1 artifact as a regular Marketplace release; pass the R1 gate on
two consecutive release candidates.
